macro.regime: Hawkish Fed tightening colliding with an AI-concentration risk-off shock
macro.narrative: Two straight inflation prints (hot core CPI at +0.3% m/m, matching Waller's own 50bp-consideration threshold, and a PPI report whose annual rate hit a four-year high of 6.5%) have pushed CME FedWatch to price a December hike as essentially certain (~88.5% 25bp/~11.5% 50bp), with the DXY at a 19-month high and the 10Y yield near 5.15%. That hawkish repricing collided over the week with an idiosyncratic shock: Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation as Nvidia CEO amid an espionage/affair scandal (which he confirmed in a Sunday Nov 15 statement) wiped over $800B off NVDA and dragged the whole semiconductor complex down 5-10% on Friday -- a jolt the Fed's own Financial Stability Report (Nov 13) context-stamped by naming AI the top-cited systemic risk (87% of contacts, up from 50% in spring) against $1.1T+ of compute-linked debt. Crypto is the cleanest real-time barometer of the resulting risk aversion: BTC has fallen from Friday's $68,249 close to roughly $63,400 by Sunday morning SGT on $1.6B+ of forced liquidations, ETF outflows, and a sharp stablecoin-supply contraction. Credit stress remains concentrated in the CCC tier rather than broad-based, and China's weakening credit impulse (contracting loans, 19-month-low M2) is a separate, demand-side drag. One genuine de-escalation data point stands apart from this risk-off tilt: China's MOFCOM confirmed (9 Nov) a further extension of its rare-earth export-control truce through 10 Jan 2027, even though heavy-REE licensing (dysprosium, terbium, yttrium) remains in force. Longer-dated rate pricing is telling a 'hike now, cut later' story (markets now pricing ~3.5 cuts by Sept 2027, up from under 2 a week ago), consistent with a late-cycle regime where tightening into slowing growth and AI-capex-debt vulnerabilities raises the odds of a sharper eventual reversal.
